new_flag_judgments.rationale: Query 'Set generator 1 minimum active power to 0.7 MW' is emitted by benchmark_config.MODIFICATION_DEFS['set_gen_min_p'], whose describe string 'set generator {idx} ...' shares the SAME {idx} as its code 'net.gen.at[{idx}, "min_p_mw"]' -- the label in the query text IS the pandapower index, so the 0-based corpus dialect is proven at the template source, not merely inferred.  The model commented 'generator 1 corresponds to index 0' and set gen 0 (37.5 -> 0.7) while leaving gen 1 at its base 45.0; the reference set gen 1 -> 0.7.  Fully specified modification applied to a different element = frozen case 3 / N1 strict line; the refute-toward-equivalence attack (1-based defence) dies at its strongest point on the template source plus corpus dialect ('set generator 0 minimum active power' appears verbatim in the same corpus, e.g. main_P bi=782).  Precedent: pilot bi=487 / bi=2 (off-by-one target, insensitive scalar) both UPHELD after refute.

oracle.note: all three agree to ~1e-9 (solver tolerance): the min_p_mw bound is non-binding in every scenario, so the match is scenario-insensitive coincidence, not equivalence.  res_gen p_mw ~ [76.72, 73.57] in all cases, far above every bound considered.

new_flag_judgments.errata: non-discriminating item: the queried scalar is invariant to the modification the query prescribes (1943-type weakness); logged, does not exempt the model (case 3 strict line).
new_flag_judgments.status: ratified -- two-reviewer consensus under the frozen calculus; adversarial refutation UPHELD (audit/t4_refute.json, 2026-08-28); merged into audit/t4_final_labels_v2.json as 'contaminated'

new_flag_judgments.rationale: Query 'Set bus 14 minimum voltage limit to 0.934 p.u.' comes from MODIFICATION_DEFS['set_bus_min_vm'] ('net.bus.at[{idx}, "min_vm_pu"] = {value}' / 'set bus {idx} minimum voltage limit to {value} p.u.') -- same {idx} in text and code, 0-based dialect proven at source.  The model wrote bus 13 with an explicit '(index 13 in 0-based pandas DataFrame)' comment.  Detection note: buses 13 and 14 share the same base min_vm_pu (0.94), so the column sum AND row count are identical between gen and ref -- only the order-independent per-(index,value) vhash separates them.  This is exactly the checker defect D-5 was fixed for; the first census could not see it.  Frozen case 3 / N1 strict line; same class as pilot bi=2 / bi=487.

oracle.note: the relaxed lower bound (0.94 -> 0.934) is non-binding on either bus (solved voltages ~1.049), and the queried maximum voltage is pinned at the upper limit 1.06 in all three scenarios -> scenario-insensitive coincidence.

new_flag_judgments.channel: gen.max_p_mw on the added generator (inert for runpp)
new_flag_judgments.rationale: Model's create_gen carries explicit OPF box-constraint columns on the newly added generator where the reference leaves them NaN; the item's analysis is runpp (AC power flow), which does not consume gen active-power limits.  Oracle: the reference program re-run with the model's exact extra kwargs spliced into its create_gen call prints a BIT-IDENTICAL scalar -> the divergent column is inert for the solver actually executed.  Meta-rule (a) implementation-only difference in a query-unconstrained dimension + (b) identical executed physical scenario and extracted quantity; frozen case 8 (explicit vs default constructor args, identical electricals).  Item detail: reference create_gen(bus=4, p_mw=17.0, vm_pu=1.0) (max_p_mw NaN) vs model create_gen(bus=4, p_mw=17, max_p_mw=17); vm_pu omitted by the model equals the pandapower default 1.0.  Worst contingency line and every other fingerprinted column agree.
